notable_absence.finding: No RBAC/privilege section on this page - keyspace hints are query-planning directives layered on top of whatever statement they're embedded in, so they inherit that statement's privilege requirements rather than having their own.

cross_component_finding: The page repeatedly asserts a mutual-exclusivity constraint that doesn't fit any existing relation shape: 'you cannot use a hint comment and the USE clause to specify optimizer hints on the same keyspace. If you do this, the hint comment and the USE clause are both marked as erroneous and ignored by the optimizer' (stated near-identically for INDEX, INDEX_FTS, USE_NL, and USE_HASH). This is a syntax-level restriction, not a privilege/edition/deployment/UI-mode gate or a cost tradeoff, so it wasn't forced into a mint - noted here as a finding instead. Also confirms, from this page's own side, the isSynonymOf pairs already captured on join.json for USE_HASH/USE HASH and USE_NL/USE NL (hint-comment form vs. inline ANSI JOIN clause form).
